paper.title_en: Black hole shadows and weak gravitational lensing in charged bumblebee gravity: Plasma effects and EHT constraints
paper.abstract_en: We investigate photon motion, black-hole shadows, weak gravitational lensing, and image magnification for a charged static black hole in bumblebee gravity immersed in dispersive plasma environments. The bumblebee field introduces spontaneous Lorentz-symmetry breaking through the dimensionless parameter <math altimg="si97.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1567"><mi>L</mi></math>, while the electric charge is characterized by <math altimg="si99.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1572"><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>. Photon propagation is treated with the Hamiltonian formalism for a cold non-magnetized plasma. A homogeneous plasma and a non-uniform power-law profile are used in the photon-sphere and shadow analyses, while homogeneous and singular-isothermal-sphere (SIS) plasmas are considered in the weak-lensing analysis We first determine the allowed black-hole domain from the horizon condition and then compute the photon-sphere radius, optical shadow radius, EHT-compatible angular shadow size, weak deflection angle, and magnification observables. The results show that increasing the charge-to-mass ratio decreases the photon-sphere and shadow radii and suppresses the weak deflection angle, while the Lorentz-violating parameter produces a milder but systematic reduction of these observables through its coupling to the charge sector. Plasma dispersion shifts the photon sphere outward but reduces the apparent shadow radius; in contrast, its effect on weak lensing depends on the plasma profile, enhancing the homogeneous-plasma deflection while slightly suppressing the SIS-plasma deflection. We further confront the theoretical shadow with the Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87* and Sgr A*. The EHT angular diameters, <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1582"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">M87∗</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>42</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">as</mi></mrow></math> and <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1607"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Sgr A∗</mi></mrow></msub><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>48.7</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>7</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">as</mi></mrow></math>, translate into exclusion regions in the <math altimg="si49.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1631"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> parameter space and show that charge, Lorentz violation, and plasma dispersion are strongly degenerate in shadow-based tests. These results demonstrate that simultaneous use of shadow constraints, weak deflection, and magnification can provide complementary probes of Lorentz-violating charged black-hole spacetimes in realistic plasma environments.
